messages.author: 7a0d46cfe7d661bf
messages.subject: Define a distribution in PySTAN
parts:
Hello, 

I would like to know if it is possible to define my own distribution using PySTAN. I searched a lot on google but did not get meaningful results. Here's an example:

Consider that my likelihood = p1 * p2 

where p1 = 0                                                   if x < 5
                = ( log(x) - log5 ) / (log19 - log5)     if 5 < x < 19
                = 1                                                   if x > 19

and knowing that x = m^2 * n^(-1/3) * o^(-3/2) * p^(-1/6)

and p2 = 0.32 * n^(-2/3) * o * p^(-1/3).

I want to marginalize over m, n, o, and p. Is it possible to implement this in PySTAN?

Thanks !

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Define a distribution in PySTAN
parts:
> On Jun 8, 2015, at 7:38 PM, Paula Sarkis <paula.s...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello,
>
> I would like to know if it is possible to define my own distribution using PySTAN.

Yes. The modeling language is independent of interface, so what works
in PyStan will also work in the other Stan interfaces.
> I searched a lot on google but did not get meaningful results.

The manual has several examples, but it's a PDF. We've been meaning to
make it more searchable. See the chapter on user-defined functions. There
are examples of how to define a probability function that can be used with sampling notation.

> Here's an example:
>
> Consider that my likelihood = p1 * p2
>
> where p1 = 0 if x < 5
> = ( log(x) - log5 ) / (log19 - log5) if 5 < x < 19
> = 1 if x > 19

It wasn't clear to me what the domain of x being considered
was --- is x continuous or discrete, constrained or unbounded?
This won't be a proper probability function (density or mass) in any
case because it's not normalized.

> and knowing that x = m^2 * n^(-1/3) * o^(-3/2) * p^(-1/6)
>
> and p2 = 0.32 * n^(-2/3) * o * p^(-1/3).
>
> I want to marginalize over m, n, o, and p. Is it possible to implement this in PySTAN?

I'm a bit lost here as to what you're trying to do. What are the
arguments to the density?

May I ask why you're trying to create these density functions?

- Bob
